'''Jozef Dravecký''' (25 July 1947 – 23 January 2023) was a Slovak mathematician and diplomat. Between 1991 and 2013, he served as the ambassador of Slovakia to Bulgaria (1993–1998), the [[Baltic states|Baltic State]]s (2000 – 2005) and the [[Holy See]] (2007–2013).<ref name="Dw">{{cite web |title=Profile at Dravecky's family website |url=https://www.dravecky.org/osobnosti/ |access-date=24 January 2023}}</ref> 

Dravecký was born in [[Spišská Nová Ves]]. <ref name="postoj">{{cite web |last1=Magušin |first1=Michal |title=Zomrel Jozef Dravecký / Od matematika a člena tajnej cirkvi až po veľvyslanca vo Vatikáne |url=https://www.postoj.sk/68614/od-matematika-a-clena-tajnej-cirkvi-az-po-velvyslanca-vo-vatikane |website=www.postoj.sk |access-date=24 January 2023 |language=sk}}</ref> He studied Sciences at the [[Comenius University]] graduating in 1971. In 1973 – 1990 he was a professor of [[Mathematical analysis|Mathematical Analysis]] at the university.<ref name="Dw" />

In 2010, Dravecký was awarded the [[Order of Pope Pius IX|Knights Grand Cross of the Order of Pope Pius IX]] by the Pope [[Pope Benedict XVI|Benedict XVI]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Slovenský veľvyslanec dostal vysoké vyznamenanie od pápeža |url=https://domov.sme.sk/c/5381487/slovensky-velvyslanec-dostal-vysoke-vyznamenanie-od-papeza.html |website=domov.sme.sk |access-date=24 January 2023 |language=sk}}</ref>

His death, on 23 January 2023 at the age of 75, was announced by the Chairman of the Christian Union of Pensioners Peter Mach in a Facebook post.<ref name="postoj" />
